Description

Noxious stimuli and inflammatory mediators open TRPV1 and ATP-gated P2X3 and P2X2/3 channels on the nerve endings in the joint, which lets sodium and calcium in and potassium out. The resulting depolarisation opens voltage-gated sodium channels, NaV1.8 among them, and the nerve fires action potentials towards the spinal cord. NaV1.7 amplifies small depolarisations to the threshold for firing, NaV1.8 carries most of the upstroke, and people born without NaV1.7 feel no pain. Blocking TRPV1, NaV1.8 or P2X3 reduces joint afferent firing and pain behaviour in osteoarthritis models.
